extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, reviewers, and students of literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for conducting fair, philosophical, and evidence-based literary criticism, and criteria for evaluating poetic quality (with examples drawn from Wordsworth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and philosophical inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a fair and philosophical inquisition into the character of the poet on the evidence of published works; prefer a positive, not merely comparative, appreciation of characteristic excellencies, deficiencies, and defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announce and endeavour to establish the principles which you hold for the foundation of poetry in general, then apply those principles to the works being reviewed. Avoid purely comparative or gratuitous dismissals; base judgments on stated premises and reasoned argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare critical canons up front
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic should announce and endeavour to establish the principles (canons) of criticism and specify their application to different classes of poetry before judging particular works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare canons of criticism grounded on universal morals and philosophic reason; this allows readers to follow the critic’s logic and adopt or reject conclusions based on transparent premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularize with textual exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceed to particularize the most striking passages to which your principles are applicable, using extracts from the work as evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faithfully note the frequent or infrequent recurrence of similar merits or defects and use quotations to illustrate points. Anti-pattern: making claims about a work without citing concrete passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish characteristic from accidental
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish what is characteristic of the author’s work from what is accidental or isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a fault or beauty is diffusely present across the oeuvre or only occasional; note whether defects are woven into the fabric of the work or are loose and separable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground judgments in argument, not assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid substitution of assertion for argument; do not deliver arbitrary or petulant verdicts unsupported by argument or textual quotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support verdicts with reasoned deduction and quotations; show the general rules or principles from which you deduce fault or merit. Anti-patterns: broad reproach without a single citation; pre-conceived verdicts illustrated by cherry-picked lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present errors and claims in tangible form
rubrics_metrics.description: If the critic has erred, present those errors in a definite place and tangible form so they can be detected and judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your premises and deductions explicit; this invites correction and enables constructive dialogue rather than vague denunciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid personal allusions and unlicensed personality
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude personal allusions and attacks; criticism should address the work, not private traits or extra-literary knowledge of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using knowledge beyond the author’s publications to injure reputation converts censure into personal injury and degrades the critic into gossip or backbiter. Keep focus strictly on published material and arguments derivable from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read thoroughly before judging
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not write a critique before having fully read the work; avoid illustrating preconceived opinions by cherry-picking passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: preparing a critique in advance and then pricking passages with a pin to support preconceived views. Ensure the review reflects the work as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and weigh the intended effect of criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic must know what effect he intends to produce and, with that object in view, weigh his words accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose tone strategically: severity or mildness are permissible when addressing the work, but they should be deliberate. Reckless personal bitterness is unjustified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be faithful to announced editorial plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect the publication’s announced plan (e.g., review only works fit for argumentative criticism) and avoid deviating to attack trivial works or pump up sales by indulgence of malign passions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticisms of trivial or juvenile works can indicate personal spite or a mercenary motive to increase circulation; avoid such breaches of editorial fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base institutional criticism on shared code
rubrics_metrics.description: If critics act as a corporate body (journals, societies), they should lay aside individuality and administer judgment according to a constitution or code grounded in universal morals and philosophic reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective judgments acquire dignity if made as representative of a body under agreed principles; avoid factional or partisan exercises presented as corporate pronouncements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate character–genre congruity
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether characters and modes (e.g., a vagrant merchant) are congruous with the poem’s genre and essential constituents (e.g., a lofty didactic poem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a character's life, imagery, and experiences suit the poem’s aims; incongruity is a legitimate ground for criticism when it undermines the poem’s effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconstancy of style
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistency of style: avoid sudden and unprepared transitions from lines of peculiar felicity to undistinguished or prosaic language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware abrupt sinks from elevated poetic diction into neutral prose that cause anticlimax or jarring alternation. Example anti-patterns include juxtaposing a noble couplet with mundane, conversational lines without smoothing transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage poetic diction vs prose diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Be mindful of the three species of language—peculiar to poetry, proper to prose, and neutral—and avoid improper mixing; the writer should raise the lower tints so the elevated passages cohere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The technique is to elevate surrounding neutral language so the poet’s high moments sit naturally; failure produces disappointment when the metre reminds the reader of promises the text does not fulfill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select the dignified and happiest attitude of things
rubrics_metrics.description: The office and duty of the poet is to select the most dignified as well as the gayest, happiest attitude of things; the reverse belongs to burlesque and travesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poets aiming at loftiness should avoid adopting a taste for burlesque or frivolous travesty that would be considered a mark of degraded taste unless that is the explicit aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value distinctive diction and memorable lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctive diction (syntactic peculiarities like asymartaeton, apposition; characteristic polysyllabic choices) and lines that can be quoted for their independent weight are marks of authorial genius and poetic value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizability of voice and extractability of lines (passages that stand alone in beauty or force) are positive criteria. Examples cited: 'The Child is father of the Man' and other short memorable passages. Antipattern: dismissing such lines as unintelligible without engaging their context or usage.
